How to Use the Item Guide

Use this collection for questions about something you already own: which trousers suit a top, which shoes work with a skirt, or where an outfit gains unwanted visual weight. Before choosing an aesthetic, identify the
main garment's shape
, then assess proportions, layers, and style. Solve the garment you are actually wearing rather than forcing the wardrobe into one label.
For an upper-body garment, explore the
the women's tops guide
. For waist rise, leg width, or trouser length, use the
Women's Trouser Guide
. For dresses and skirts, begin with the
Skirt and Dress Guide
; if the outfit nearly works but feels too heavy or lacks an anchor, explore the
Footwear Guide
or
Women's Alternative Accessories
1. Identify the silhouette
Is the main garment fitted, straight, roomy, or voluminous? Balance the next piece through proportion as well as color.
2. Assess visual weight
Dense fabrics, substantial boots, hardware, and many layers add weight; lighter details and open areas can reduce it.
3. Choose the style afterward
The same base can lean Goth, E-Girl, Baddie, or Dark Feminine through footwear, outerwear, and accessories.
